title.text: Blink the firefly needs your help, Maven. So do his friends.
There are 10 chapters and 80 puzzles: riddles, mazes, matching games, patterns, and number puzzles.
Earn up to 3 stars on every puzzle. Play a chapter again and its puzzles and mazes change.

start.text: You are snug in bed, Maven. Ella the elephant is under one arm. Sharky the shark is under the other.
The house is quiet. A full moon hangs outside your window, as round and white as a dinner plate.
Something tiny is knocking on the glass. You pull back the curtain. It is a firefly! But his light is very dim, like a flashlight with tired batteries.
My name is Blink. I am lost. I need to get home to the Lantern Tree before my light goes out.
This is Ella, and this is Sharky. How do you get to the Lantern Tree?
But every helper on the road asks a riddle. And they are not easy ones. I am terrible at riddles. Are you any good?
You grin. You are very good at riddles.
Here is a firefly secret. We glow brighter near bright ideas. Every riddle you solve will make my light stronger. I need eight of them to shine all the way home.
You put on your slippers. You tuck Ella under one arm and Sharky under the other. Then you tiptoe outside.
The grass is cool and wet on your ankles. Crickets are singing. Two paths lead away from your yard. One goes into the dark trees. One runs beside the water.

woods.text: The trees are tall here. Their leaves whisper, shh, shh, shh, as if the whole forest is trying to fall asleep.
Blink flies ahead. His light is so small that you can hardly see your own slippers. Little hard things crunch under your feet.
In the crook of a great oak tree sits an owl with round gold eyes.
Whooo goes there?
she asks.
A lost firefly and his three friends,
you say.
We are looking for the Lantern Tree.
The owl turns her head almost all the way around to look at Ella and Sharky.
An elephant and a shark in my woods,
she says.
Now I have seen everything. I know the way. But first, tell me what this is.
I am smaller than your thumb, and I wear a little cap.
A giant is folded up inside me.
Plant me and wait, and the giant will stand taller than a house.
What am I?
A mushroom.
An egg.
An acorn.
A sunflower seed.
The answer is: An acorn.
You think about the little hard things under your slippers. You pick one up. It is wearing a tiny brown cap.
An acorn!
The owl blinks slowly.
Clever. This whole oak tree was once folded up inside an acorn no bigger than your thumb.
Blink’s light glows a little brighter.
That was a bright idea!
he says.
The owl points one wing up the path.
The road splits ahead. Blueberry Hill is up high. The Hollow Log is down low. Both will take you onward.
Which way do you go?
Climb Blueberry Hill.
Crawl through the Hollow Log.
A mushroom is small and wears a cap. That part fits. But there is no giant inside. A mushroom stays small. Try again!
An egg has a baby animal folded up inside. But an egg wears no cap, and nothing grows if you plant one. Try again!
So close! A sunflower grows tall, but not taller than a house. And its seed has a striped shell, not a cap. Try again!

hill.text: You climb up, up, up. Blink rides on your shoulder. Ella and Sharky ride in your arms.
The trees end, and the sky opens wide above you.
At the top, a hare lies on her back in the clover. Her long ears are spread out like a pillow. She is looking straight up.
Four hundred and six,
she mutters.
Four hundred and seven. Oh, bother. Now I have lost my place.
What are you counting?
asks Blink.
I count them every night,
says the hare.
I always fall asleep before I finish. You tell me what they are. Then I will show you the way down.
We are up there all day, but the sun hides us.
The darker it gets, the better we show.
We look like cold little sparks, but each of us is a fire bigger than the whole world.
What are we?
Fireflies.
The windows of a faraway town.
Stars.
Snowflakes.
The answer is: Stars.
You lie down in the clover next to her and look up. Ella and Sharky look up too.
Stars!
you say.
Yes,
Each star is a giant ball of fire. They only look small because they are so very far away. In the daytime they are still up there. The sun is just too bright for us to see them.
The sun is a star too,
she adds.
It is only the closest one.
She points one long ear down the far side of the hill.
Follow the path into the brambles. Mind the weaver. She is fussy about her work.
Go down into the brambles.
Blink giggles. Not me! I show up better in the dark, but I am tiny up close too. And my light is not a fire. Try again!
Faraway windows do look like little sparks at night. But a window is not a fire bigger than the world. Try again!
Snowflakes are cold and little. But they really are little. These things only look small because they are very far away. Try again!

log.text: The Hollow Log is as wide as a tunnel, and very long. Inside it is as dark as a pocket.
You hold Ella and Sharky tight. Blink’s little light is almost gone. Dry leaves crunch under your slippers.
Then you see a warm glow ahead. It is a hedgehog, holding a tiny lantern on a stick.
Mind your step,
he says.
There are roots. I will light your way to the end of the log. But first, answer me this.
I am joined to your feet, but you can never step on my head.
Lift the lantern high, and I shrink.
Set the lantern on the ground, and I stretch out long.
Blow the lantern out, and I am gone.
What am I?
Your reflection.
Your footprints.
An echo.
Your shadow.
The answer is: Your shadow.
May I hold the lantern?
you ask. The hedgehog hands it over.
You lift it high. A short dark shape huddles at your feet. You set it on the ground. The dark shape shoots all the way down the log.
My shadow!
you say.
Right you are,
says the hedgehog.
No light, no shadow. Low light, long shadow.
You wiggle Ella’s trunk. A giant dark trunk wiggles on the wall. Sharky’s shadow has very big teeth.
The hedgehog leads you through to the far end.
Out here and into the brambles,
Mind the weaver. She is fussy about her work.
Walk into the brambles.
Your reflection lives in mirrors and in still water. There is no mirror in this log. Try again!
Footprints are made by your feet. But they stay behind when you walk away, and they do not need a lantern. Try again!
An echo is a sound. Moving a lantern up and down cannot make a sound longer or shorter. Try again!

web.text: The path dips into a thicket of brambles. The branches bend over your head and make an arch.
You are about to walk through when Blink squeaks,
Stop!
You freeze. Right in front of your nose, something silver is stretched across the arch from side to side. Drops of dew hang on it like tiny glass beads.
In the very middle sits a small gray weaver. She has more legs than you can count in a hurry.
Thank you for stopping,
she says.
The last visitor walked straight through my night’s work. It was a badger. It took me until morning to fix.
We are sorry about the badger,
you say.
Is there a way around?
There is. But first, tell me what you nearly walked into.
I am a trap with no teeth and a net with no knots.
My maker carried every bit of the thread inside her own body.
The wind blows right through me, but a fly cannot.
What am I?
A fishing net.
A cocoon.
A spider web.
A bird cage.
The answer is: A spider web.
You look at the silver threads. You look at the weaver and count her legs slowly this time. Eight.
A spider web!
Just so,
says the spider.
Every thread came out of me. No knots, no needle, and all of it made since sunset.
Sharky thinks a trap with no teeth is a very strange idea.
The spider points one thin leg at a gap low in the brambles.
Crawl under there. You will come out at the tall hedge. Look for the Round Door.
Crawl under the brambles.
A fishing net is full of knots. And its thread came from a shop, not from inside its maker. Try again!
Good thinking! A caterpillar does spin a cocoon with thread from its own body. But a cocoon is a snug sleeping bag, not a trap. Wind cannot blow through it. Try again!
A bird cage has bars, not thread. And a fly can zip right between the bars. Try again!

stream.text: The stream sparkles in the moonlight. It chatters over the pebbles like someone telling a long story.
You hold Sharky up for a good look. Sharks love water.
But the stream is too wide to jump, and you do not want wet slippers.
An old turtle rests on the bank with his chin on a stone.
Looking for a way across?
he asks, very slowly.
There is one close by. I have used it for a hundred years. Tell me its name, and I will tell you where it is.
I have one foot on each bank, but I never take a step.
I am over the water, but I am not a bird.
Travelers walk across my back, and I stay right where I am.
What am I?
A rainbow.
A boat.
A heron.
A bridge.
The answer is: A bridge.
You think about feet, and backs, and banks.
A bridge!
you say.
The turtle nods, very slowly. It takes a long time.
Just past the reeds.
Blink’s light glows a little brighter.
That was a bright idea!
he says.
You cross the little wooden bridge. Your slippers go clomp, clomp, clomp. Ella looks over one side. Sharky looks over the other.
On the far side, the road comes to a wide, still pond. The Lantern Tree is somewhere past it.
How do you cross the pond?
Hop across the stepping stones.
Ride the lily pad raft.
Great thinking! A rainbow curves over the water with one end on each side. But nobody can walk across a rainbow. Try again!
A boat carries travelers. But a boat sits in the water, not over it. And it moves. Try again!
A heron stands very still by the water. But a heron is a bird, and nobody walks across its back. Try again!

stones.text: Four stones sit in a row at the edge of the pond. From left to right, there is a gray stone, a white stone, a speckled stone, and a black stone.
A frog watches you from a lily leaf. Her throat goes in and out.
Careful,
she croaks.
Only one of those stones starts the real path. The other three wobble and tip. Splash!
You do not want a splash. Ella does not like getting wet. Sharky would not mind at all.
Which one is it?
you ask.
I will give you two clues,
says the frog.
You need both of them. Think before you hop.
Clue one: the steady stone is not at either end of the row.
Clue two: the steady stone is not next to the black stone.
Which stone do you step on?
The gray stone.
The white stone.
The speckled stone.
The black stone.
The answer is: The white stone.

You point at each stone in turn. The gray stone and the black stone are at the ends, so they are out. That leaves the white one and the speckled one. But the speckled stone sits right next to the black one. So it is out too.
You step onto the white stone. It holds as still as a table.
Well worked out,
Most visitors just guess. Most visitors get wet.
More stones rise up in a neat row. Hop, hop, hop. You are across. A muddy slide runs down the bank ahead, and somebody is whistling.
Follow the whistling.
The gray stone is at the left end of the row. Clue one says the steady stone is not at an end. Try again!
The speckled stone is not at an end, so it fits clue one. But look what is right beside it. Try again!
The black stone is at the right end of the row. Clue one says the steady stone is not at an end. Try again!

raft.text: A fat green lily pad bobs by the bank. It is as big as a rug.
All aboard,
says a sleepy duck.
No splashing. No standing up. No sharks in the water.
She gives Sharky a long look.
You sit down in the middle with Ella and Sharky safe in your lap. The duck pushes the lily pad along with her beak. The water goes lap, lap, lap.
Halfway across, she stops. The pond is as smooth as glass.
Look around you,
she says.
It is riddle time.
There is only one of me, but tonight you can see two.
One is too high to reach.
The other is close enough to touch. But touch it, and it breaks into wiggly pieces.
Leave it alone, and it mends itself.
What am I?
A bubble.
A star.
A fish.
The moon.
The answer is: The moon.
You look up. A bright white circle hangs high over the trees. You look down. There it is again, floating beside the lily pad.
You dip one finger into the water. The circle breaks into wiggly ribbons. Then it slides back together.
The moon!
you say.
Yes,
says the duck.
The pond is like a mirror. There is one moon, up in the sky. The other one is only its picture.
She pushes you the rest of the way. On the far bank, a muddy slide runs down to the water, and somebody is whistling.
Follow the whistling.
Touch a bubble and it does break. But it pops for good. It never mends itself. Try again!
There is not only one star. There are too many to count! Try again!
A fish is close enough to touch. But there are lots of fish in a pond, and a fish does not break into pieces. Try again!

otter.text: Whee! Splash! An otter zooms down the muddy slide on his belly. He pops up out of the water right at your feet.
He climbs out and shakes himself. Then he sees Sharky and jumps a little.
Is that a shark?
Sharky is a very gentle shark,
you say.
Sharky only eats pretend fish.
Good,
says the otter.
Because I am a bit short of fish tonight, and I cannot work out why. Help me with my fish problem, and I will show you the path to the tall hedge.
He holds up three small fish by their tails.
Tonight I caught some fish.
I gave half of them to my sister.
Then I ate 2 myself.
Now I have 3 left.
How many fish did I catch?
The answer is: 10.
You work it out backward. He has 3 fish now. Before he ate 2, he had 5. And those 5 were only half. The other half went to his sister. So that is 5, and 5 more.
Ten!
You caught 10 fish.
The otter counts on his paws.
Five for her. Five for me. Two in my tummy. Three in my paw. You are right! Nobody took any. I just ate them.
He points his tail up the bank.
Follow the path through the tall grass. You will come to the tall hedge. Look for the Round Door.
Take the path to the hedge.
You cannot share 5 fish fairly in half. Here is a hint. Before he ate 2, he had 5. And those 5 were only half. Try again!
Test it. Half of 8 is 4. He eats 2. That leaves 2 fish, not 3. Try again!
Test it. Half of 12 is 6. He eats 2. That leaves 4 fish, not 3. Try again!

door.text: The hedge is taller than your house. It is too tall to climb and too thick to squeeze through. It goes left and right as far as you can see.
But in the middle is a round wooden door. It has a brass knocker shaped like an acorn.
A sign on the door says:
knock the right number of times.
Oh dear,
says Blink.
I always knock the wrong number. Then it will not open until tomorrow.
Under the sign, in small curly letters, is a riddle.
I am less than 20.
You say me when you count by threes.
You say me when you count by fives.
What number am I?
The answer is: 15.
You count by threes on your fingers. 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. Then you count by fives. 5, 10, 15. Only one number is in both lists.
Fifteen!
you say.
You knock fifteen times. It takes a while. Blink counts along so you do not lose your place.
The round door swings open without a sound.
Behind it is a garden, silver in the moonlight. A white stone path goes two ways. One way leads to a mossy stump with a tiny light on it. The other way leads to an old stone well.
Which way do you go?
Visit the mossy stump.
Look into the old well.
Count by fives: 5, 10. Yes! Now count by threes: 3, 6, 9, 12. You skip right over 10. Try again!
Count by threes: 3, 6, 9, 12. Yes! Now count by fives: 5, 10, 15. You skip right over 12. Try again!
Count by threes: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. Yes! Now count by fives: 5, 10, 15, 20. You skip right over 18. Try again!

stump.text: On top of the mossy stump sits a worm. He wears glasses no bigger than two drops of dew. He is reading a leaf. A glowworm holds very still above him for a lamp.
Shh,
says the worm, without looking up.
I am at the good part.
You wait. Ella waits. Sharky waits. Blink does not wait very well.
At last the worm turns his leaf over.
I am a bookworm,
he says.
I love words. I love the letters inside them even more. You look like a reader. Are you a reader?
Yes,
you say.
Then this one is for you.
I am a letter.
You can find me in frog and in hedgehog.
I am in moon two times.
What letter am I?
G.
N.
O.
R.
The answer is: O.
You spell the words in your head. frog and hedgehog both have a G and an O. But moon has no G at all. And it has two Os, right in the middle.
The letter O!
Oh, yes,
says the bookworm. He looks very pleased.
And look up. Tonight the moon is shaped like one, too.
He points his tail down the white path.
The Lantern Tree is just past the roses. Good night, reader.
Walk past the roses.
G is in frog and in hedgehog. Good! But now look at moon. There is no G in it. Try again!
N is in moon, but only one time. And there is no N in frog. Try again!
R is in frog. But there is no R in hedgehog or in moon. Try again!

well.text: The old well is made of round gray stones. A wooden bucket hangs over it on a rope.
You stand on your tiptoes and look in. It is very deep and very dark. You cannot see the bottom. You take a big breath to call down.
A little brown bat is hanging upside down under the roof of the well.
First, guess what lives at the bottom,
Then you may call down and see if you are right.
I have no mouth, but I answer you.
I only know the words you just gave me.
I say them softer, and a little late.
says the well, softer and a little late.
says the well. Ella wants a turn too.
I use echoes to find my way in the dark,
I squeak, and I listen for my squeak to bounce back. That is how I know where the trees are.
She points one wing down the white path.
And that is how I know the Lantern Tree is just past the roses.
A parrot copies your words. But a parrot has a beak to talk with, and it loves to speak first. Try again!
Your shadow copies you, and it has no mouth. But a shadow never makes a sound. Try again!
A bell has no mouth, and it rings back when you hit it. But a bell cannot say your words. Try again!

tree.text: Past the roses is a meadow. In the middle stands the biggest tree you have ever seen. Its branches spread wider than your whole house. But it is dark from top to bottom.
Oh no,
says Blink.
Everyone is asleep already.
Not everyone,
says a creaky little voice. An old firefly floats down from a branch. Her light is soft and steady.
Blink! We looked for you everywhere.
Grandma Glow!
Blink zips in a happy circle around her.
Thank you, Maven,
says Grandma Glow.
And thank you, Ella and Sharky. Now, shall we wake the tree? It asks one riddle first. It always has.
The leaves rustle. A deep, slow voice seems to come from everywhere at once.
Give me away, and you still have just as much of me.
I can jump from one candle to the next, and then both have me.
One puff of breath can end me.
What am I?
A cookie.
A secret.
A flame.
A balloon.
The answer is: A flame.
You think of birthday candles. One candle can light the next, and the first one burns just as bright. And one puff blows them out.
A flame!
you say.
Just so,
says the deep voice.
Light is a thing you can give away and still keep.
It works for firefly light, too,
Watch.
Blink touches his glowing tail to the nearest leaf. A light wakes up there. That light wakes two more. Then ten. A hundred. A thousand. Soon the whole tree shines like a golden lantern.
Grandma Glow lands on your thumb.
You brought our Blink home. Now we will take all of you home.
How would you like to go home?
Float home on a dandelion puff.
Ride home in a leaf boat.
Give a cookie away and you have less cookie. This thing does not get smaller when you share it. Try again!
Clever! When you share a secret, you still have it. But a secret cannot jump onto a candle. Try again!
A puff of breath makes a balloon bigger. It does not end it. And if you give a balloon away, it is gone. Try again!

puff.text: Grandma Glow picks a dandelion puff as big as an umbrella. You tuck Ella and Sharky into your pajama top. Then you hold on to the stem with both hands.
A thousand fireflies blow all together. Whoosh! Up you go.
You float over the garden and the round door. You float over the water and the woods. Everything below looks small and soft, like a blanket with trees stitched on it.
Blink flies beside you. His light is strong now.
My first one ever! It took me the whole trip. Want to hear it?
I spend all night in bed, but I never sleep.
I have a case, but I never go on a trip.
All day I do nothing. At night, I hold up just one part of you.
Blink does a happy loop in the air.
I was proud of the case part.
Down below, you can see your own house and your own window. The curtain is still open.
A suitcase is a case. But it goes on lots of trips, and it does not spend the night in your bed. Try again!
A mattress is in bed all night. But it holds up all of you, not just one part. Try again!
A blanket stays in bed. But it lies on top of you. It does not hold up any part of you. Try again!

leaf.text: The fireflies lift a big curled leaf. You climb in with Ella and Sharky. It fits the three of you just right.
A thousand tiny lights carry you up. You sail over the garden and the round door. You sail over the water and the woods. The leaf rocks like a cradle. Ella’s ears flap a little in the wind.
Blink sits on your knee. His light is strong now.
I made up a riddle,
he says.
My first one ever! It took me the whole trip. Want to hear it?
I show you pictures, but I have no screen and no pages.
You make me yourself, but I can still surprise you.
You can only watch me with your eyes shut.
By breakfast, you may have forgotten me.
What am I?
A book.
A drawing.
A dream.
A movie.
The answer is: A dream.
A dream!
you say.
You got it!
Blink does a happy loop in the air.
I was proud of the surprise part. You make your own dreams, but you never know what will happen next.
It was the best part,
And look,
says Blink.
A good one is waiting for you.
Down below, you can see your own house and your own window. The curtain is still open.
Glide down to your window.
A book shows you pictures. But a book has pages, and you need your eyes open to read it. Try again!
You make a drawing yourself. That part fits. But you cannot see your drawing with your eyes shut. Try again!
A movie shows you pictures. But a movie needs a screen, and you watch it with your eyes open. Try again!

home.text: The fireflies set you down by your window, as soft as a feather. Then they drift away, one by one, back toward the Lantern Tree.
You climb into bed with Ella on one side and Sharky on the other. The blanket is still warm.
Blink floats at the glass. He is shining as bright as a little star.
One last riddle,
he whispers.
It is my favorite. Here is a hint. The answer is very, very close to you.
You do me thousands of times a day, and you almost never notice.
I am over faster than you can say my name.
Each time, the whole world goes dark, but you do not miss a thing.
What am I?
A breath.
A heartbeat.
A yawn.
A blink.
The answer is: A blink.
You think. Then you look at the little firefly at your window, and you smile.
A blink,
you say.
It is your name!
It is my name!
says Blink, and he glows his brightest yet.
Then you yawn. It is a big, slow one. Blink catches it and yawns too.
Now do one more blink for me,
A very slow one. Close your eyes, and do not finish it until morning.
Good night, Blink.
Good night, Maven. Good night, Ella. Good night, Sharky. Thank you for bringing me home.
His light drifts away over the grass. It gets smaller and smaller, until it looks like one more star.
You close your eyes. Your pillow is soft. Ella and Sharky are close. A good dream is waiting.
Chapter 1 is done. Good night.
You do breathe thousands of times a day without noticing. But the world does not go dark when you breathe. Try again!
Your heart beats thousands of times a day. But the world does not go dark when it beats. Try again!
Nobody yawns thousands of times a day. And a yawn is long and slow. Try again!

c2_0.text: The next night, you are almost asleep when you hear it again. Tap. Tap. Tap.
It is Blink! His light is bright tonight, but his face is worried.
Grandma Glow has lost her glasses in the Hedge Maze. Without them she cannot read bedtime stories to the baby glowworms. And nobody at the Lantern Tree is as good at puzzles as you.
You tuck Ella under one arm and Sharky under the other. Out the window you go.

c2_1.text: The Hedge Maze has a tall iron gate. It is locked. A snail is sliding slowly across the latch.
I know how to open it,
says the snail.
The answer is hanging on a hook right beside you. But you must name it first.
I have teeth, but I never chew.
I turn, but I never get dizzy.
A locked door listens to me, and to nobody else.
What am I?
A comb.
A clock.
A key.
A bell.
The answer is: A key.
A key!
you say. There it is, on a little hook under the ivy. You turn it. Click.
Slow and steady,
That is how to win a maze.
Open the gate.
A comb has teeth and never chews. But a door does not care about a comb. Try again!
The wheels inside a clock have teeth, and they turn. Good thinking! But a locked door does not listen to a clock. Try again!
A door may have a bell. But a bell has no teeth, and it does not turn. Try again!

c2_2.text: Green walls rise up on every side. Blink zips ahead and then zips right back.
Three baby glowworms wandered in here looking for Grandma’s glasses,
Can you pick them up on the way through?
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door.
You come out the far side of the hedges. The baby glowworms ride on Ella’s back.

c2_3.text: A field mouse in a straw hat is counting on her paws.
I planted 4 rows of carrots. Each row had 3 carrots. Then a rabbit ate 5 of them. How many do I have left? Tell me, and I will show you the way on.
Three and three and three and three is 12,
The gardener hides the key along one of these two paths. One is narrow and twisty. One is wide and long.
Five is how many the rabbit ate. How many did she plant first? Try again!
Count the rows again. 3 and 3 and 3 and 3 makes 12. Then take away 5. Try again!
Twelve is how many she planted. Now take away the 5 that the rabbit ate. Try again!

c2_4a.text: The hedges squeeze in close. Somewhere in here is the key to the inner gate.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. The door is locked until you find the key.
The key turns in the inner gate. You are nearly at the middle of the maze.

c2_4b.text: The path is wide here, but it goes on and on. Somewhere along it is the key to the inner gate.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. The door is locked until you find the key.
The key turns in the inner gate. You are nearly at the middle of the maze.

c2_5.text: In a little square stands a stone table with a metal fin on top. Numbers are carved around its edge. A sleepy tortoise is leaning on it.
Nobody looks at this old thing at night,
I tell the time, but I have no hands and I never tick.
My only moving part is a shadow.
At night, I am no use at all.
The sun makes a shadow, and the shadow points at the hour.
That is why I nap here.
A clock tells the time. But it has hands, and it ticks all night long. Try again!
A shadow is the moving part. But a shadow by itself cannot tell you the time. Try again!
The moon is out at night. This thing is no use at night. Try again!

c2_6.text: A garden gnome sits on a bench with twelve cards face down.
I will tell you where, if you can match all my pairs.
Tap two cards. If they match, they stay. Find all 6 pairs.
The shiny thing is in the flower bed. Look for the pattern.

c2_7.text: The flower bed is planted in a pattern: a rose, then two seeds still waiting to grow, over and over. The last spot is covered by a big leaf.
What is under the leaf in the last spot?
You lift the leaf. Under it is a seed. And next to the seed lies a little empty glasses case.
Go to the middle of the maze.
After each rose come two seeds. Only one seed has come so far. Try again!
There are no acorns in this pattern. Try again!
There are no mushrooms in this pattern. Try again!

c2_8.text: In the very middle of the maze stands a scarecrow. He is wearing a straw hat, an old coat, and something that does not belong to him.
I only wanted to see the stars better. But first, tell me what they are.
I have two windows, but no walls.
I sit on a nose and hold on to two ears.
Look through me, and blurry things turn clear.
The answer is: A pair of glasses.
The scarecrow hands them down. Blink flies them straight to Grandma Glow.
There you are, Maven. And Ella. And Sharky. Now, who wants a story?
You listen to one story with the baby glowworms. Then the fireflies carry you home to bed. Ella and Sharky are already asleep.
Windows belong in walls. These two windows sit on a nose. Try again!
Your eyes do the looking. But they do not sit on your nose or hold on to your ears. Try again!
Grandma Glow reads books. But a book has no windows, and it does not sit on a nose. Try again!

c3_0.text: Tap. Tap. Tap. Blink is back, and he is dripping wet.
The Pearl Lamp has rolled into the deep end of the pond,
It is the night-light for all the baby fish. They cannot sleep without it. I cannot swim. But I know someone who can.
You look at Sharky. Sharky looks very brave.
At the edge of the pond, an old frog blows a bubble as big as a room. You step inside with Ella and Blink. Sharky swims beside you with a happy flick of the tail. Down you go.

c3_1.text: Little silver balls drift up past you. A water beetle rows over.
Then tell me what those are.
I am round, and I am made of air inside a thin wet skin.
I always travel up, never down.
Touch me, and I am gone.
Mind the reeds. They are a maze down here.
A balloon is round and full of air. But its skin is dry rubber, and one touch does not end it. Try again!
A raindrop is round and wet. But it travels down, not up. Try again!
An egg has a thin shell. But it is not full of air, and it does not float up. Try again!

c3_2.text: Tall reeds grow up from the mud like the bars of a cage. Sharky swims ahead to find the way.
Three baby fish are lost in here, each with a tiny light.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door.
Out of the reeds! The baby fish follow Sharky in a neat little line.

c3_3.text: A whole school of fish swims by. Their teacher, a carp with tiny glasses, is counting.
Half of them turned left at the rock. Three of those hid in the weeds. How many of the left-turners can I still see?
How many left-turners can she still see?
The whole school blows bubbles at you.
Swim down to the sunken log.
Ten fish turned left. But 3 of them hid. Try again!
Half of 20 is 10. Take 3 away from 10. Do not add. Try again!
Only half the class turned left. Start with half of 20. Try again!

c3_4.text: On a sunken log sits something small and green, kicking its legs.
I was not always like this,
Guess what I am, and I will tell you where the lamp rolled.
When I was a baby, I had a tail and no legs.
Now I have legs and no tail.
I began my life under the water, and now I can hop out of it.
You used to be a tadpole.
The lamp rolled down into the Dark Deep. Two ways go down. Pick one.
Which way do you go down?
A fish begins life under the water. But it keeps its tail and never grows legs. Try again!
A turtle has legs from the day it hatches. And it keeps its little tail. Try again!
A butterfly changes a lot as it grows. But it was never a baby under the water. Try again!

c3_5a.text: It is black down here. Blink presses against the wall of the bubble. His light shows only a little way ahead.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. It is dark. You can only see close to Blink.
A soft glow shines ahead. You are nearly there.

c3_5b.text: It is black down here. Blink presses against the wall of the bubble. His light shows only a little way ahead.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. It is dark. You can only see close to Blink.
A soft glow shines ahead. You are nearly there.

c3_6.text: Shells lie in a row on the sand. Each one has a number scratched on it. The last shell is turned over.
What number is on the last shell?
Each one is double the one before,
The last shell flips over by itself. Sixteen.
The numbers do not go up by ones. Each number is double the one before. Try again!
From 4 to 8 is not plus 2. Each number is double the one before. Try again!
Each number is double the one before. Double 8 is not 12. Try again!

c3_7.text: Four gems sit in a row on the pond floor. From left to right, they are red, white, blue, and gold.
The Pearl Lamp is buried under one of them. I will give you two clues.
Clue one: it is somewhere to the left of the blue gem.
Clue two: it is not under the red gem.
Which gem do you dig under?
The answer is: The white gem.
Red and white are to the left of blue. It is not red. So it must be white.
Sharky digs nose-first. Something round and bright rolls out of the sand. The Pearl Lamp!
The red gem is to the left of the blue one. But clue two says it is not the red gem. Try again!
The lamp is to the left of the blue gem, not under it. Try again!
The gold gem is to the right of the blue gem. Clue one says left. Try again!

c3_8.text: A huge old catfish blocks the way back up. His whiskers are as long as your arm.
if you can name the thing that is all around you.
I have no color, but I can look blue.
I have no shape of my own. I take the shape of whatever holds me.
You are inside me right now, and you drink me every day.
says the catfish, and he moves aside.
Sharky carries the Pearl Lamp up, very gently, between two rows of teeth, and sets it back on its rock. All over the pond, baby fish close their eyes.
The big bubble floats you to the top and pops. Soon you are home in bed, a little damp. Sharky sleeps with a big toothy smile.
Air has no color and no shape. But you breathe air. You do not drink it. Try again!
A shadow has no color of its own. But you cannot drink a shadow. Try again!
You are inside a bubble. But a bubble has its own round shape, and you do not drink it. Try again!

c4_0.text: Tap. Tap. Tap. Blink is at the window. Beside him on the sill sits a mole with dirt on her nose.
The Glow Seed has fallen down her tunnels. It is the seed of the next Lantern Tree. If we do not find it, there will never be a new tree.
It is very dark down there,
I do not mind. I cannot see much anyway. But you will need your firefly.
You, Ella, and Sharky follow her to a hole under the old apple tree. Down you slide.

c4_1.text: Thick brown ropes hang down from the roof of the tunnel. Moss pats one.
Do you know what these are?
I am the part of a tree that never sees the sun.
I drink all day, but I have no mouth.
The tree stands tall only because I hold on tight in the dark.
I use them like street signs. Left at the big one.
A worm lives in the dark. But a worm has a mouth, and it does not hold up a tree. Try again!
An acorn can become a tree. But it does not drink all day or hold on tight. Try again!
A mushroom grows in dark places. But it is not part of a tree, and it does not hold one up. Try again!

c4_2.text: The tunnels twist every which way. Blink’s light shows only the walls right beside you.
Three glow pebbles mark Moss’s favorite spots.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. It is dark. You can only see close to Blink.
says Moss. That is a big thing for a mole to say.

c4_3.text: Moss stops at a little room full of jars.
I dug 3 on Monday. On Tuesday I dug twice as many as Monday. On Wednesday I was tired, and I dug only 1.
No wonder my paws are sore.
Tuesday was twice as many as Monday. Twice 3 is 6, not 3. Try again!
Do not forget the one tunnel on Wednesday. Try again!
Twice 3 is 6. Now add 3, and 6, and 1. Try again!

c4_4.text: The next room sparkles. Twelve flat stones lie face down on the floor.
I play by smell. You may use your eyes.
Tap two cards. If they match, they stay. Find all 6 pairs.
Now I trust you with the deep tunnels.

c4_5.text: Orange points poke down through the roof like a row of teeth. A fat grub is nibbling one.
Do not tell the gardener. Do you know what I am eating?
I grow down into the dark while my green hair grows up into the light.
I am orange, but I have never seen the sun.
To pick me, you pull me up by my hair.
The grub points with his tail.
A shiny seed? It rolled down past the crystals. There are two ways. Both are locked by an old iron grate.
Roots grow down in the dark. But they are not orange, and nobody picks them. Try again!
A mushroom has no green hair. Try again!
A flame is orange. But it does not grow in the ground, and you cannot pull it up. Try again!

c4_6a.text: Crystals glow in the walls, so you can see the whole cavern. The key to the grate is somewhere in here.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. The door is locked until you find the key.
The grate swings open. Something is glowing green at the end of the tunnel.

c4_6b.text: Crystals glow in the walls, so you can see the whole cavern. The key to the grate is somewhere in here.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. The door is locked until you find the key.
The grate swings open. Something is glowing green at the end of the tunnel.

c4_7.text: A row of crystals is set into the wall. One is missing.
Which crystal is missing from the end?
Red, blue, blue, green, over and over. So green comes next! You press the green crystal in. The stone door rolls aside.
Red comes after green, not after two blues. Try again!
There are only two blues in a row, and both are already here. Try again!
There is no gold in this pattern. Try again!

c4_8.text: There it is. The Glow Seed sits on a little hill of dirt, shining soft green. But an old badger is curled around it, half asleep.
One riddle, and it is yours,
he mumbles.
You have been walking in the answer all night.
I am a road with a roof.
I have two mouths, but I never eat.
Go in one mouth in the dark, and come out the other into the light.
What am I?
A bridge.
A bird cage.
A boat.
A tunnel.
The answer is: A tunnel.
A tunnel!
you say.
The badger yawns and rolls over. Ella lifts the Glow Seed with one careful trunk. It is warm.
Moss leads you up, up, up, and out under the stars. Grandma Glow plants the seed beside the Lantern Tree and pats the dirt down.
Come back in a hundred years,
she says.
It will be taller than a house.
Then it is home to bed, with dirt on your slippers.
Chapter 4 is done. Good night.
A bridge is a road. But it has no roof and no mouths. Try again!
A cage has a roof. But it is not a road, and you cannot walk through it. Try again!
A boat can carry you. But it has no roof and no mouths. Try again!

c5_0.text: Tap. Tap. Tap. Blink is at the window, pointing up.
A baby cloud named Puff has blown away from her flock,
She is stuck on the weathervane on top of the Cloud Castle. If she is not home by morning, the meadow will have no shade.
How do we get up there?
And tonight there is a very big wind.
You hold on tight. Ella spreads two big ears like gray sails. Sharky holds on to your pajamas. Up you go!

c5_1.text: You land on a stair made of cloud. Something pushes you from behind. Something whistles in your ear. But nobody is there.
says a voice like a long breath.
I have no hands, but I can take your hat.
I have no feet, but I can run across a field, and you can watch the grass bend where I go.
You can feel me and hear me, but you can never see me.
laughs the wind, and it gives you a push up the stairs.
You can hear an echo and never see it. But an echo cannot take your hat. Try again!
A shadow has no hands and no feet. But you can see it, and it makes no sound. Try again!
A balloon can run away across a field. But you can see it go. Try again!

c5_2.text: Inside the castle, the walls are fog and the floors are mist.
Three sparks of starlight are scattered in the halls.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door.
You step out onto a balcony. The whole world is far below, small and soft.

c5_3.text: A silver wire runs from tower to tower. A row of sparrows sits on it. The littlest one is trying to count.
Four flew off. Then two came back, and each one brought a friend. How many of us now?
How many birds are on the wire now?
Then 2 birds and 2 friends land. Nine again!
The sparrows think this is the best joke they have ever heard.
Two came back, and each brought a friend. That is 4 birds landing, not 2. Try again!
Count the friends too. Two birds and two friends is 4 birds landing. Try again!
Do not forget the 4 that flew away at the start. Try again!

c5_4.text: In the next room, bright shapes bob against the ceiling, each one tied down with string. A heron in a blue cap is the keeper.
I fly, but I am not alive.
I have a tail, but I am not an animal.
The harder the wind pulls me away, the tighter someone holds my string.
You will need it. The top of the castle is across the Sky Maze. Two doors lead in.
A balloon flies on a string. But it has no tail, and it does not need the wind. Try again!
A parrot flies and has a tail. But a parrot is alive. Try again!
A cloud flies and is not alive. But nobody holds a cloud on a string. Try again!

c5_5a.text: The Sky Maze is made of thin gold mist. Hold on to the kite string, and do not look down.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door.
The wind lifts the kite, and the kite lifts you, right up to the top of the tower.

c5_5b.text: The Sky Maze is made of thin gray mist. Hold on to the kite string, and do not look down.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door.
The wind lifts the kite, and the kite lifts you, right up to the top of the tower.

c5_6.text: A great dial hangs on the tower wall, with numbers that count down. The last number has blown away.
You chalk an 8 on the dial. A hatch opens above you.
The numbers do not go down by ones. Look at the jump from 20 to 17. Try again!
From 20 to 17 is 3. From 17 to 14 is 3. Take 3 from 11. Try again!
That is 4 less than 11. Each jump is only 3. Try again!

c5_7.text: Four birds have been racing around the tower all night: Jay, Dove, Wren, and Owl. Now they are arguing about who came second.
Jay, then Dove, then Wren, then Owl,
Dove bows. Owl says he was only resting his eyes.
Jay finished before Dove, and Dove was before Wren. So Jay was first, not second. Try again!
Wren finished after Dove. So Dove was ahead of Wren. Try again!
Owl finished last of all. Try again!

c5_8.text: At the very top, a small white shape is snagged on the golden weathervane, sniffling. The weathervane is a rooster, and he is cross.
I will let her go when someone tells me what she is,
he says.
I have been asking all night.
I can be white as wool or gray as a mouse.
I am heavier than an elephant, but I float.
I can hide the sun. And when I cry, the garden drinks.
What am I?
A pillow.
Snow.
A balloon.
A cloud.
The answer is: A cloud.
A cloud!
you say.
Hmph. Obviously,
says the rooster. He lifts one golden wing, and Puff floats free.
She is so happy that she rains on you a little. Ella does not like getting wet, but tonight Ella lets it go.
Puff carries all of you home on her back. It is like riding a very soft, very slow pillow. You are asleep before you land.
Chapter 5 is done. Good night.
A pillow is white and soft. But it does not float, and it cannot hide the sun. Try again!
Snow is white. But it falls down. It does not float in the sky. Try again!
A balloon floats. But it is light, not heavy, and it does not cry. Try again!

c6_0.text: Tap. Tap. Tap. There is frost on the window tonight. Blink is wearing a tiny scarf.
The Northern Lights have gone out,
They are the night-light for the whole top of the world. The Light Keeper says her Ice Bell is missing. Without it, she cannot ring them back on.
You put on your warmest robe. Ella gets a sock for a hat. Sharky gets a mitten for a sleeping bag.
A sled is waiting in the yard, pulled by six snow hares. Away you go, up the mountain.

c6_1.text: White specks drift down all around the sled. One lands on your nose. A snow hare looks back at you.
I fall a very long way, but I never get hurt.
I have six arms, and no two of us look the same.
Catch me on your tongue, and I am only a drop of water.
you say, and you catch one.
Count them if you do not believe me.
A raindrop falls a long way. But it has no arms, and raindrops all look alike. Try again!
A star has points. But it does not land on your tongue. Try again!
A spider has eight legs, not six arms. And please do not catch one on your tongue. Try again!

c6_2.text: The sled stops at a wall of blue ice. The only way on is through.
Three lost sparks of the Northern Lights flicker inside.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door.
You slide out the far side on your slippers. Wheee.

c6_3.text: Four fox cubs tumble out of a snowy den. Their mother is counting boots.
Four paws each. One boot for every paw. But three boots are lost in the snow. How many boots do we still have?
Count 4 and 4 and 4 and 4. Then take away 3. Try again!
Four cubs with four boots each is 16. Then take away 3. Try again!
Sixteen is how many boots they started with. Now take away the 3 lost ones. Try again!

c6_4.text: The foxes invite you in to warm up. On the floor are twelve chips of ice with pictures scratched underneath.
Tap two cards. If they match, they stay. Find all 6 pairs.
You are warm again, and the cubs have seen how the game is done.

c6_5.text: The path crosses a wide, flat lake. It is as hard as a floor and as clear as a window. The otter’s cousin slides past on her belly.
Do you know what you are standing on?
I am water, but you can walk on me.
I am as hard as a stone, but I float.
Hold me in a warm hand, and I cry myself away.
The best thing water ever turned into.
The Ice Bell is up at the peak,
A snowstorm is coming. Two trails go up.
A stone is hard. But a stone sinks, and it is not water. Try again!
You can walk over water on a bridge. But a bridge is not made of water. Try again!
A bubble floats. But you cannot walk on a bubble. Try again!

c6_6a.text: Snow whirls so thick that you can see only a step or two. Stay close to Blink’s light.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. It is dark. You can only see close to Blink.
The storm blows itself out. The peak is right above you, sharp against the stars.

c6_6b.text: Snow whirls so thick that you can see only a step or two. Stay close to Blink’s light.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. It is dark. You can only see close to Blink.
The storm blows itself out. The peak is right above you, sharp against the stars.

c6_7.text: Steps are cut into the rock. Each one has a letter. The top step is covered in snow.
What letter is on the top step?
A, skip B. C, skip D. E, skip F. G, skip H,
You brush off the snow. There is the letter I. And beside it, half buried, is a little silver bell made of ice.
Take the bell to the Light Keeper.
H comes right after G. But this pattern skips a letter each time. Try again!
That skips two letters. This pattern skips only one. Try again!
That skips three letters. This pattern skips only one. Try again!

c6_8.text: The Light Keeper is a great white owl. She takes the Ice Bell gently in her beak.
One last riddle before I ring it. How will you get home?
I race down the hill, but I must be dragged back up.
I have no wheels, no legs, and no engine.
The snow is my road. Without it, I only sit.
says the Light Keeper. She rings the Ice Bell. Ting.
Green and pink and purple light pours across the sky like spilled paint. All over the top of the world, little animals stop being afraid of the dark.
Your sled races all the way home under the lights. You are asleep before it stops.
A boat has no wheels and no legs. But its road is water, not snow. Try again!
A kite has no wheels. But it rides the wind, not the snow. Try again!
A snowflake comes down the hill. But nobody drags it back up. Try again!

c7_0.text: Tap. Tap. Tap. Blink is hopping from foot to foot on the windowsill.
She will be three hundred and one. I want to buy her a present at the Night Market. But the stalls only take moon coins, and you only get moon coins for solving puzzles.
The Night Market is under the old stone bridge. Paper lanterns swing on strings. Every stall has a puzzle and a jar of silver coins.

c7_1.text: A raccoon sells nuts by the scoop. On her counter stands a shiny thing with two little dishes hanging from a bar.
One coin if you can name it,
I have two arms and two dishes, but I never eat.
I cannot count, but I always know which side is heavier.
When both sides are fair, I stand perfectly level.
says the raccoon, and she drops it in your hand. It is cold and bright.
A clock has two hands, not two dishes. And it cannot tell you which side is heavier. Try again!
A bell hangs from a bar. But it has no dishes. Try again!
A bridge stands level. But it has no dishes, and it cannot tell which side is heavier. Try again!

c7_2.text: My cousin lives in a log,
Apples are 2 coins. Pears are 3 coins. Pretend you have 10 coins, and you buy 2 apples. How many pears can you buy with what is left?
How many pears can you buy with what is left?
That leaves 6. Two pears cost 6. Two pears!
says the hedgehog. Another coin. That makes two.
You can do better. After the apples you have 6 coins. How many 3s are in 6? Try again!
Three pears cost 9 coins. After the apples, you have only 6. Try again!
Four pears cost 12 coins. After the apples, you have only 6. Try again!

c7_3.text: The market is a maze of stalls and strings of lights.
Three moon coins are shining on the ground where shoppers dropped them. Finders keepers.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door.
The coins clink in your pajama pocket.

c7_4.text: A spider sells necklaces. Each string has more beads than the last.
How many beads go on my next string?
Each number is the two before it, added together,
says the spider. She pays you two coins.
The numbers do not go up by ones. Try adding the last two numbers together. Try again!
Close! Add the last two numbers: 3 and 5. Try again!
Add only the last two numbers: 3 and 5. Try again!

c7_5.text: Drip. Drip. Rain is coming through the cracks in the bridge. A duck is doing very good business at the next stall.
and I will lend you one.
I open when the sky cries, and I close when it stops.
I have ribs, but no heart.
I keep you dry by getting wet myself.
The duck gives you a coin and lends you a big green umbrella. Ella is very glad.
The present stall is behind the night gate,
The watchman hides the key. Go by Spice Row or by Cloth Row.
A cloud is what makes the sky cry. It does not keep you dry. Try again!
A mushroom is the right shape. But it has no ribs, and it does not open and close. Try again!
A blanket covers you. But it has no ribs, and a wet blanket keeps nobody dry. Try again!

c7_6a.text: Spice Row smells of pepper and cinnamon. Find the watchman’s key, and pick up any coins you see.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. The door is locked until you find the key.
The night gate creaks open. You count your coins. Almost enough.

c7_6b.text: Cloth Row is hung with flags and scarves. Find the watchman’s key, and pick up any coins you see.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. The door is locked until you find the key.
The night gate creaks open. You count your coins. Almost enough.

c7_7.text: A big brass bell hangs in the middle of the market. A sign says:
ring the right number for A prize.
I am more than 10 and less than 15.
You say me when you count by threes.
Only 12 and 14 are even. And counting by threes goes 3, 6, 9, 12. Twelve!
Dong. Dong. Dong. Twelve times. The whole market claps. The prize is a fat bag of moon coins.

c7_8.text: The last stall is run by an old toad in a velvet coat. He has music boxes, and silver thimbles, and tiny lanterns. Blink cannot choose.
The best present in my stall is not for sale,
says the toad.
Guess it, and take anything else you like.
You can give me away and still keep me.
I cost nothing, but I am worth a lot.
I am one small curve that changes a whole face.
Give me to someone, and you often get one right back.
What am I?
A secret.
A flame.
A yawn.
A smile.
The answer is: A smile.
A smile!
you say. You are wearing one.
The toad gives one right back.
Take the little lantern,
he says.
No charge.
Blink cannot wait until tomorrow. He flies the present straight to the Lantern Tree. Grandma Glow gives him the biggest smile of her three hundred years.
You can see it from your bedroom window, all the way across the meadow. Then you fall asleep, smiling too.
Chapter 7 is done. Good night.
You do still have a secret after you share it. But a secret is not a curve on a face. Try again!

You do often get a yawn right back. But a yawn is a big open circle, not a small curve. Try again!

c8_0.text: Tap. Tap. Tap. You look at your clock. It says eight. That is odd. It said eight a long time ago.
The Great Clock in the tower has run down, and all the little clocks follow it. If nobody winds it, morning will never come.
Ella and Sharky agree that this is serious. Off you go to the Clock Tower in the middle of town.

c8_1.text: A mouse in a waistcoat opens the tower door. He holds up a glass thing with sand inside.
Before you come in, tell me what I use to time my tea.
I have two rooms and one tiny door between them.
I am full of sand, but I am not a beach.
When my top room is empty, your time is up. Flip me over, and it starts again.
The answer is: A sand timer.
A clock tells time. But it has no sand and no rooms. Try again!
A sundial tells time with a shadow, not with sand. Try again!
You can time an egg with it. But an egg has no sand inside. Try again!

c8_2.text: The bottom of the tower is packed with wheels and gears, all standing still. You have to squeeze between them.
Three bright little springs have popped loose. The clock will need them.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door.
The springs are safe in your pocket.

c8_3.text: Halfway up, a bat hangs beside a row of bells.
But I have lost track. When the clock stopped, it was 7 o’clock. Then I napped for 2 hours and ate moths for 1 hour. What time should it be now?
Seven and 2 is 9. One more is 10,
That is only 1 hour after 7. She napped for 2 hours and ate for 1. Try again!
That counts her nap. Now add the hour she spent eating. Try again!
That is 4 hours after 7. She napped for 2 and ate for 1. Try again!

c8_4.text: On the next landing, someone has left a cake with candles. A cuckoo pops out of a little door in the wall.
Cuckoo! It is nobody’s cake until the clock starts,
Guess what kind of day is stuck.
I come once a year, but I am not a season.
Everybody has one, and nobody can borrow yours.
Each time I visit, your number goes up by one.
She cannot turn three hundred and one until the clock moves.
Two stairways go up from here.
Winter comes once a year. But winter is a season, and everybody shares it. Try again!
A full moon comes about once a month, not once a year. Try again!
Candles come with it. But a candle is not a day. Try again!

c8_5a.text: The stairs are pitch dark, and they twist and split like a maze.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. It is dark. You can only see close to Blink.
You come out high up, behind the giant clock face. The moon shines through the glass numbers.
Step out behind the clock face.

c8_5b.text: The stairs are pitch dark, and they twist and split like a maze.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. It is dark. You can only see close to Blink.
You come out high up, behind the giant clock face. The moon shines through the glass numbers.
Step out behind the clock face.

c8_6.text: The Clock Mouse keeps his tools up here, and a set of worn old cards.
The winding key is under one of these pairs,
I forget which. Match them all.
Tap two cards. If they match, they stay. Find all 6 pairs.
Under the last pair is a big brass winding key.
Carry the key to the clock.

c8_7.text: To set the clock, the mouse hops around the giant clock face. He lands on 1, then 4, then 7, then 10. Then he stops, puzzled.
After 12, a clock starts again at 1.
The mouse lands on the 1. Something deep in the tower goes clunk.
He hops 3 numbers each time, not 1. Try again!
From 10, hop three numbers: 11, 12, and then one more. What comes after 12 on a clock? Try again!
That is four hops from 10. He hops only three. Try again!

c8_8.text: The Great Clock itself speaks, in a voice like a slow drum.
Wind me, and I will run. But first, tell me what it is that I count.
I never stop, and I never go back.
Clocks can count me, but they cannot hold me.
You can spend me, save me, or waste me, but you can never buy more.
You fit the springs back in. You turn the big brass key. Tick. Tock. Tick. Tock.
All over town, clocks start again. Far away in the meadow, Grandma Glow turns three hundred and one.
But first it has to be bedtime.
You can spend, save, or waste money. But you can get more of it, and clocks do not count it. Try again!
The wind stops sometimes. This never does. Try again!
A river keeps going. But clocks do not count rivers. Try again!

c9_0.text: Tap. Tap. Tap. Blink is at the window. Riding on his back is a worm in tiny glasses.
There has been an accident at the Library of Lost Words. Somebody sneezed. All the letters blew out of the books. I need a reader to help me put them back.
The library is inside a hollow hill. Its shelves go up and up, out of sight. Loose letters drift in the air like snow.

c9_1.text: Three letters are spinning above the front desk. The Bookworm squints at them.
This word fell out of a book about owls,
I am a word with three letters.
Read me forward or backward, and I do not change.
You have two of me on your face.
E, Y, E. It is the same both ways.
The three letters zip back into the book about owls.
You do have two ears. But read ear backward and you get rae. Try again!
mom is the same forward and backward. But you do not have two of them on your face. Try again!
pop is the same forward and backward. But you do not have two of them on your face. Try again!

c9_2.text: The shelves make narrow halls that turn and turn.
Three bright letters have rolled far into the stacks.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door.
The letters are back where they belong.

c9_3.text: In a soft chair sits a very old moth, asleep with a book on her lap. Something thin is sticking out of the pages.
Just tell me what it is.
I am as thin as a leaf, and I sleep between pages.
I never read a single word.
But I always know exactly where you stopped.
she says, and she goes back to sleep.
A book has the pages. This thing sleeps between them. Try again!
I read every word! says the Bookworm. Try again!
A pillow is for sleeping. But it is not thin, and it does not fit in a book. Try again!

c9_4.text: Four letters lie on a table, spelling star. The Bookworm frowns.
This page was about animals. Try reading it the other way.
Read it backward, from the last letter to the first.
Four letters scurry back to their page. A picture of rats waves at you.
The oldest books are locked in the Deep Stacks,
The key is on one of two floors.
Go down to the Lower Stacks.
arts uses the same letters. But it is not star read backward. Start with the R. Try again!
There is no C in star. Try again!
That is mixed up, not backward. Start with the last letter, R. Try again!

c9_5a.text: Dust lies thick up here. Find the key to the Deep Stacks, and gather any letters you see.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. The door is locked until you find the key.
The old lock opens with a sound like a book closing.

c9_5b.text: Dust lies thick down here. Find the key to the Deep Stacks, and gather any letters you see.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. The door is locked until you find the key.
The old lock opens with a sound like a book closing.

c9_6.text: The stair down to the Deep Stacks has a letter on every step. The last one is worn away.
What letter is on the last step?
Z, skip Y. X, skip W. V, skip U. T, skip S,
You step on the R. A door swings open.
S comes right before T. But this pattern skips a letter each time. Try again!
That skips two letters. This pattern skips only one. Try again!
That skips three letters. This pattern skips only one. Try again!

c9_7.text: A desk stands in the Deep Stacks, with paper ready. A yellow stick with a pink tip lies beside it. A cricket is the clerk here.
The more I work, the shorter I get.
I wear a little hat that fixes my mistakes.
I am full of words that nobody has written yet.
The last book has lost its very first words.
A candle gets shorter as it works. But it has no hat that fixes mistakes. Try again!
A book is full of words that are already written. Try again!
A drawing is what you make with it. Try again!

c9_8.text: The biggest book in the library lies open. Its first page is blank. You hold the pencil. The Bookworm holds his breath.
Write what I am,
whispers the book.
I can be told a thousand times and never wear out.
I live in a book, but I also live in a voice in the dark at bedtime.
I often begin with once and finish with the end.
You are inside one right now.
What am I?
A song.
A dream.
A story.
A secret.
The answer is: A story.
You write: once upon A time.
A story,
sighs the book. All through the library, letters fly home to their pages like birds to their nests.
Thank you, reader,
says the Bookworm.
You may borrow any book you like. Forever.
You pick one. But you are asleep before the fireflies get you home. Ella holds your place.
Chapter 9 is done. Good night.
A song can be sung a thousand times. But it does not begin with once. Try again!
A dream comes in the dark at bedtime. But nobody can tell the same dream a thousand times. Try again!
Tell a secret a thousand times, and it is not a secret anymore. Try again!

c10_0.text: Tap. Tap. Tap. But tonight it is not the window. Something bright has landed in your yard with a soft thump.
You run outside with Ella and Sharky. Blink is already there. In the grass sits a very small star, holding one of her points and crying sparkly tears.
I leaned out too far to watch you solve riddles. Now I cannot get home, and the sun comes up soon. Stars cannot be on the ground when the sun comes up.
Blink whistles. From the woods, the pond, the tunnels, and the clouds, your friends start to come.

c10_1.text: The owl from the Whispering Woods swoops down first. She points one wing. At the top of Blueberry Hill, something tall and silver is leaning against the sky.
Whooo can tell me what it is?
I have two long legs, but I never walk.
Between my legs are many steps, and you climb every one.
I lean against things, but I am never tired.
It only shows up when a star needs it. Climb fast.
A heron has two long legs. But a heron walks, and nobody climbs one. Try again!
You walk across a bridge. You do not climb it, and it does not lean. Try again!
A spider has eight legs, not two. And you should not climb one. Try again!

c10_2.text: The ladder goes up into a tangle of low clouds. There it splits into a hundred little ladders.
Three of the star’s sparkles are caught in the mist.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door.
Above the clouds, the air is cold and clear. The little star rides on Ella’s head.

c10_3.text: The otter is here, holding on to a rung.
I climbed 8 rungs. I slipped back 3. Then I climbed 6 more. What rung am I on? I have lost count again.
Eight take away 3 is 5. Now add 6. Try again!
Do not forget the slip. Eight take away 3 comes first. Try again!
He slipped back 3. Take them away. Do not add them. Try again!

c10_4.text: Halfway up there is a bench made of cloud. Puff the baby cloud has saved it for you.
Your friends have left a matching game on the seat.
Tap two cards. If they match, they stay. Find all 6 pairs.
The little star claps her points. She has stopped crying.

c10_5.text: A huge dark cloud sits right across the ladder. There is no way around it. Inside, you can see nothing but Blink.
I am bright enough now. You made me that way.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. It is dark. You can only see close to Blink.
You burst out of the top of the cloud. The stars are so close that you could count their points.

c10_6.text: The Bookworm is waiting with three little boxes: gold, silver, and blue.
The star’s missing sparkle is in one of these,
he says.
Each box has a note on it. But be careful. Only one of the three notes is true.
Gold box: The sparkle is in here.
Silver box: The sparkle is not in here.
Blue box: The sparkle is not in the gold box.
Only one note is true. Which box holds the sparkle?
The gold box.
The silver box.
The blue box.
The answer is: The silver box.
You test each box. If the sparkle is in the silver box, the gold note is false and the silver note is false. Only the blue note is true. One true note!
You open the silver box. The sparkle jumps out and sticks itself back on the little star’s point.
The hardest one yet,
says the Bookworm,
and you worked it out.
The Sky Gate is just above,
says Blink.
It is locked at night. Two ways lead to the key.
Which way do you go?
Go by the Milky Way.
Go by the Moon Path.
Test it. If it is in the gold box, the gold note is true. But then the silver note is true too. That is two true notes. Try again!
Test it. If it is in the blue box, the silver note is true, and the blue note is true. That is two true notes. Try again!

c10_7a.text: This is the top of everything. Find the key to the Sky Gate. Morning is coming.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. The door is locked until you find the key.
The Sky Gate swings open. Behind it is the Moon, as big as a house and as kind as a grandmother.

c10_7b.text: This is the top of everything. Find the key to the Sky Gate. Morning is coming.
Slide your finger along the path to lead Blink, or tap the arrows. Pick up the 3 green lights, then go to the gold door. The door is locked until you find the key.
The Sky Gate swings open. Behind it is the Moon, as big as a house and as kind as a grandmother.

c10_8.text: you are home. And you, Maven. You have solved riddles on the road, under the pond, in the dark, in the clouds, on the mountain, in the market, in the tower, and in the library.
I am not a thing you can buy or build.
You cannot be one all by yourself. It takes two.
Share a trouble with me, and it gets smaller. Share a joy with me, and it grows.
You have one under each arm.
You look at Ella. You look at Sharky. You look at Blink, and the owl, and the otter, and all the rest.
The little star hops up into her place in the sky and shines. She is the bright one just over your house. Look for her tomorrow.
The Moon carries you down herself and tucks you in. Ella on one side. Sharky on the other. Blink glows at the window like a night-light.
The End. You finished the whole game!
It takes two to share a secret. But a secret does not make a trouble smaller. Try again!
A smile is free, and it is good to share. But you can smile all by yourself. Try again!
A shadow stays with you. But you cannot share a joy with a shadow. Try again!
